Subject: POC kickoff & hands-on demo — coordinating US/EU/APAC windows

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We’re excited to get the hands-on POC started. Our team spans the US, London, and Singapore offices — the main ask from our side is to run an initial prompt review + routing deep dive and then a 30–45 minute warmup load test during the same engagement.

Constraints:
- VP of Engineering (John Tan) is only available afternoons PT / mornings CET.
- Our APAC team prefers sessions between 07:00–10:30 SGT.
- We’d like a rotating schedule so the burden of odd hours isn’t always on the same engineers.

Can you propose a cadence that gives each region a chance at reasonable local hours (we’re OK with one rotating evening session per region)? Also include a quick checklist for what we should prepare on our side.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Jacobs
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp
(External)

Emily — great to hear. Draft proposal below and I’ve attached an .ics with the first rotation for calendar import. High level: three-week rotating blocks where each week focuses on a different ‘priority’ timezone for the hands-on window, plus a short overlap window for cross-region sync.

Week structure (90-minute hands-on + 30-minute buffer for follow-ups):
- US-priority week: 13:00–14:30 PT (works for late morning EST) + 20:00–20:30 CET overlap
- EU-priority week: 15:00–16:30 CET + 22:00–22:30 SGT overlap
- APAC-priority week: 08:00–09:30 SGT + 16:00–16:30 PT overlap

Load test: 30–45 minute window during the hands-on block; we’ll coordinate exact token budget and traffic shape in advance.

Prep checklist for Acme:
- 2–3 prompt examples and expected outputs (CSV or Google Doc)
- A short list of routing scenarios you want us to emulate (region, model fallback, quantized variant)
- A point-of-contact for infra/networking (to whitelist our load test IPs)

Attachments: rotational_windows_v2.ics (calendar import).

If that looks reasonable I’ll loop in Jordan to align on test harness and Marissa to run the prompt calibration session before the hands-on.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

Rafael — quick internal note for the thread before we send the final plan to Acme.

Notes for the prompt review and routing deep dive (what we should cover):
- Prompt review (30–40m): canonical prompts, edge-case prompt set, deterministic vs. sampled decoding expectations. Bring a handful of failing examples.
- Routing (20m): show policy-based routing by region + automatic fallback to quantized variant (we should demo failover latency differences).
- Load test (30–45m): plan a ramp up to 100 RPS for 3 minutes and a sustained 25 RPS for 5 minutes — include both cached and cold-start patterns.

Action items: Jordan to validate the load harness and provide a short runbook we can share with Acme. Karthik to prepare suggested quantization profile for their expected token distributions. I’ll draft the customer-facing runbook and share links.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-loadtest-playbook

Marissa
Manager, Technical Customer Programs
